metaTitle: 3-Day Nanjing Itinerary (2026): Prices & What to Book
metaDescription: Three days in Nanjing: Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum free but booked online, Ming Xiaoling ¥70, Qinhuai boat ¥80–100, and what closes on Mondays.
heading: 3-Day Nanjing Itinerary for First-Time Visitors (2026)

byline.name: Maintained by Lin
byline.tested: Prices, hours and booking rules checked against official sources, October 2026

quickAnswer: For three full days in Nanjing:

items: **Day 1:** the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum and Ming Xiaoling, in the Zhongshan scenic area.
**Day 2:** Nanjing Museum or the Presidential Palace, then the Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall. It's a solemn historical site, so give it time.
**Day 3:** the city wall, the Confucius Temple area and the Qinhuai River.

quickAnswer: Watch out for Mondays: the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, Nanjing Museum and the Memorial Hall all close on Mondays, with holiday exceptions. The mausoleum is free but needs an online booking, and Ming Xiaoling is ¥70. Book the museum and each Memorial Hall exhibition area separately, with your passport, and check whether your train uses Nanjing or Nanjing South station.

blocks.text: **Getting to Zhongshan.** Take Metro Line 2 to Muxuyuan station, Exit 1: Ming Xiaoling is about 500 m away and the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum about 1 km. Sightseeing buses also run to the mausoleum from Muxuyuan and Xiaolingwei stations.

items: A reservation for one Memorial Hall exhibition area does not admit you to all three. The main Massacre Historical Exhibition and Three Victories area are adjacent but have different entrances; Liji Lane is farther away.

Choose the exact exhibition area in the booking system and save its confirmation and entrance. Keep the same original passport available for document checks; a screenshot of a passport does not replace the original document.
If no suitable museum or memorial slot is available, change the sightseeing order or choose another activity. Do not build the day around an assumed walk-in place.
Give the memorial an unhurried, respectful visit. Check venue-specific age and accessibility rules before adding Liji Lane, and leave room to shorten the day if the material is distressing.

items: The Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, Nanjing Museum and the Memorial Hall all close on Mondays, so Monday is the day for the city wall and the Qinhuai area. If both the museum and the memorial matter to you, book compatible slots first; otherwise move one to Tuesday and shorten the Zhongshan day.

For other weekday combinations, move the museum and memorial block to an open day and keep each confirmed booking. Check the mausoleum on its own rather than treating every Zhongshan sight as one schedule.

Opening hours and closures are in the [tickets table](#tickets), checked against official sources in October 2026. Holiday hours apply only on their stated dates, and your booking confirmation decides entry.

Take Metro Line 2 to Muxuyuan station, Exit 1. Start with the Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum: it's free but needs an online booking in your passport name, it's open 8:30–17:00, and it's closed on Mondays except national holidays. The tomb chamber itself isn't open to visitors.
Be ready for stairs and a long outdoor walk. If mobility or weather makes the climb unsuitable, spend more time in an accessible part of the scenic area instead.

Add one substantial second stop. Ming Xiaoling (¥70) is about 500 m from Exit 1. The ¥100 combined ticket also covers Linggu, the Music Stage and Meiling Palace, but don't try to see them all in one relaxed day.
Ming Xiaoling is part of the UNESCO-listed Imperial Tombs of the Ming and Qing Dynasties. Read a little of its history before you go, and take your time on the tree-lined approach.
Head back into the city for dinner. A full Qinhuai evening on top of two big eastern sites is too much for one relaxed day.

Choose Nanjing Museum for regional history or the Presidential Palace for a different focus. Use the separate-reservation comparison above if choosing the museum, including its foreign-passport service-centre procedure, and secure a time that leaves room for the rest of the day.
Leave a proper midday break before the Memorial Hall of the Victims in Nanjing Massacre by Japanese Invaders. Its exhibitions cover traumatic events and deserve time and respectful attention.

For the Memorial Hall, select the actual exhibition area and keep its own reservation confirmation. Follow the official visitor guide and the entrance for that booking; do not assume one reservation covers all three areas.
Keep the rest of the day light. If you prefer not to visit the memorial, use this block for a second museum or a quieter neighbourhood without implying the sites are interchangeable.
Allow travel time between the city-centre museum options and the memorial. End near your hotel rather than scheduling an unrelated distant attraction.

sections.title: Day 3: walls, southern lanes and Qinhuai

items: Explore one accessible section of Nanjing's city wall or Zhonghua Gate after checking the specific entry point and ticket rules. The walls are long; choose a segment rather than planning a complete circuit.

Walk through the southern old city toward the Confucius Temple area (free to walk, though some sights charge; Metro Line 3, Fuzimiao station). Look into the side streets and local food rather than staying on the busiest shopping frontage.
Walk by the Qinhuai River in daylight or early evening. The painted-boat trip boards near the Confucius Temple: ¥80 by day (9:00–18:30) or ¥100 at night (18:30–22:00).
If you have a late train, keep this day flexible, collect your luggage and allow time for security at your exact station.

sections.title: Where to stay and how to arrive

items: Stay near a useful metro interchange in the central city if you want balanced access to Zhongshan, the museums and Qinhuai. A hotel in the Qinhuai area suits evening walks but means a longer trip east.
Nanjing and Nanjing South are different railway stations. Check the station printed on your ticket; Shanghai also has several departure stations.

Book on 12306 or Trip.com, with your details exactly as in your passport. Tickets go on sale 15 days before departure, and China Railway's FAQ confirms foreign passengers can use their passports for real-name tickets. [How to book China trains](/china-train-travel-guide/)
If you're flying in, check the airport-to-city metro or road route and your hotel's late check-in. Save the hotel's Chinese name and address offline.

Before you book a hotel, check its "Guests Accepted" line on Trip.com ([how](/china-hotels-for-foreigners/#check-before-booking)), and check the nearest metro station and a realistic travel time to the sights.

sections.title: Adapt the route to your interests

items: With one day, choose either Zhongshan's mausoleum area or the museum and southern old city. Adding the memorial should be a deliberate decision with enough time.
With two days, keep Zhongshan on one day and a museum, the memorial and Qinhuai on the other, trimming the list if admission times conflict.
For families or limited mobility, reduce stairs and walking, choose one major site per half-day and confirm accessible entry and transport.

If museums matter most, give the Nanjing Museum a generous block and move the Presidential Palace to another day or another visit. If food and neighbourhoods matter most, spend more of Day 3 beyond the busiest Qinhuai frontage.

faqs.question: How do foreign-passport visitors enter Nanjing Museum?
faqs.answer: Make a real-name reservation through the official museum WeChat mini-program. The museum visitor page directs foreign-passport holders to bring the original passport used for booking and successful-reservation proof to the service centre green-channel window before entry. Check current notices for your date.

faqs.question: What should I do in Nanjing on Monday?
faqs.answer: The Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum, Nanjing Museum and the Memorial Hall all close on Mondays, with holiday exceptions. For a Monday–Wednesday visit, use Monday for the city wall and the Qinhuai area, Tuesday for Zhongshan, and Wednesday for a confirmed museum or memorial visit. If both the museum and the memorial are priorities, book compatible slots or shorten the Zhongshan day.

faqs.question: Does one Memorial Hall reservation cover all three exhibition areas?
faqs.answer: No. The official guide requires separate reservations. The main Massacre Historical Exhibition and Three Victories area are near Yunjin Road but use different entrances; the Liji Lane venue is farther away near Daxinggong. Select the area you intend to visit and follow its confirmation.

faqs.question: Are three days enough for Nanjing?
faqs.answer: Yes for one Zhongshan day, one museum and remembrance day, and one old-city and Qinhuai day. Allow more time for several museums or distant excursions.

faqs.question: Which railway station should I use in Nanjing?
faqs.answer: Use the exact station on your ticket. Nanjing and Nanjing South are different stations and require different transfers.

faqs.question: Do I need to reserve Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's free, but you need an online, real-name booking; passports are accepted. It's open 8:30–17:00 and closed on Mondays except national holidays, and the tomb chamber itself isn't open to visitors.

faqs.question: Can foreigners visit the Nanjing Massacre Memorial Hall?
faqs.answer: The memorial's official visitor guide lists passports among valid documents. Check the current reservation channel and visiting rules before going, and allow an unhurried, respectful visit.

faqs.question: Can I visit Ming Xiaoling and Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum on the same day?
faqs.answer: Often yes with an early start and suitable entry arrangements, but both involve walking and may have different tickets. Choose only those two main sites for a manageable Zhongshan day.

faqs.question: Can ChinaEase Buddy customise the three days?
faqs.answer: Yes. Share your arrival station, dates, hotel, mobility, museum interests and memorial preference so the route fits your actual visit.

faqs.question: How much do Nanjing's main sights cost?
faqs.answer: The Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum is free with an online booking, and the Confucius Temple area is free to walk, though some sights charge. Ming Xiaoling is ¥70, or ¥100 for a combined ticket with Linggu, the Music Stage and Meiling Palace. A Qinhuai River boat is ¥80 by day and ¥100 at night. Nanjing Museum and the Memorial Hall need advance bookings.
